# Recipes

A recipe is a verified [`http`](plan-format.md#the-generic-http-adapter) spec for one operation of one provider,
shipped with Sponson: the line names it and fills in its params, and the requests, envelopes, ids and drift rules
come from the recipe. Everything the generic adapter guarantees holds unchanged (intents before creates, idempotent
apply, drift by hash, destroy only what Sponson created). Why and how: [ADR 0020](adr/0020-recipes.md).

```yaml
providers:
  http:
    cloudflare: { recipe: cloudflare }   # optional: the recipe's API defaults; override base_url, auth, headers here
changes:
  - id: preview_dns
    adapter: http
    op: resource                         # the recipe's kind: resource or list_item
    recipe: cloudflare.dns_cname
    zone_id: 023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353
    name: "${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com"
    target: preview-host.example.net
```

- `recipe: <provider>.<op>` picks the operation; `api` defaults to `<provider>`, and so does its block under
  `providers.http`: write the block only to override `base_url`, `base_url_env`, `auth`, `headers` or `encoding`.
- Every other key of the line is one of the recipe's params. Values are literals, `${ctx.*}`, `{ from }`,
  `{ secret }` or `{ keep: true }`, as anywhere in a plan. An unknown param, a missing required one or a value of
  the wrong type is `PARAM_INVALID` naming it, before any request; an unknown recipe or op lists the known ones.
- `destroy: keep` leaves what the line made in place when the scope is destroyed.
- Identity: the ledger records the API block as resolved (base URL, credential variable, headers, encoding) and the
  keys and record ids of the expanded requests, never the recipe's text. A line written by hand with the same
  values is the same resource, and a new Sponson version whose recipe changes only its docs, params or assumptions
  re-identifies nothing.

Every op below is tested by `scenarios/recipes.test.ts` against the local fake cloud (create, idempotent re-apply,
drift, destroy), and live with `pnpm test:live` when its credential and the `SPONSON_LIVE_*` variables its recipe
names are set.

| Recipe | Op | What it manages | Credential |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`cloudflare.dns_cname`](#cloudflaredns_cname) | `resource` | DNS CNAME record | `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (bearer) |
| [`turso.database_branch`](#tursodatabase_branch) | `resource` | Database branch | `TURSO_API_TOKEN` (bearer) |

## Cloudflare

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/cloudflare.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/cloudflare.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Create DNS record](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/create/)
- [List DNS records](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/list/)
- [DNS record details](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/get/)
- [Update DNS record (PATCH)](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/edit/)
- [Delete DNS record](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/delete/)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4` |
| `base_url_env` | `CLOUDFLARE_API_URL` |
| Credential | `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **CF1** (verified, [source](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/create/)): Records are created with `POST /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records` (`type`, `name`, `content`, `ttl`, `proxied`, `comment`), authenticated with an API token as `Authorization: Bearer` that has DNS Write on the zone.
- **CF2** (verified, [source](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/list/)): `GET /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records` answers `{ result: [...] }` and filters by `type` and `name.exact` (names compare case-insensitively).
- **CF3** (verified, [source](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/get/)): Single-record answers (create, details, update) carry the record under `result`, with its `id`.
- **CF4** (verified, [source](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/delete/)): `PATCH /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records/{id}` updates a record; `DELETE` on the same path removes it permanently.
- **CF5** **(unverified)**: A PATCH needs `name` and `type` alongside the changed fields (the edit schema does not mark them optional), so every update sends both.
- **CF6** **(unverified)**: The API returns `name` lower-cased as the full name and `content` as written, so `name` must be given lower-case and fully qualified, or every plan finds no record and tries to create one.
- **CF7** **(unverified)**: A proxied record reports `ttl: 1` (automatic) whatever was sent, so `ttl` other than 1 with `proxied: true` shows as drift on every plan.
- **CF8** (verified, [source](https://developers.cloudflare.com/api/resources/dns/subresources/records/methods/create/)): A CNAME cannot share its name with another record, so name and type identify it within the zone and a filtered list holds at most one, on its first page.

### `cloudflare.dns_cname`

**DNS CNAME record** (`http.resource`). A CNAME record in a zone, such as `pr-42.preview.example.com` pointing at the preview deployment's host. Located by name and type; a console edit of its target, proxying, TTL or comment is drift.

Covers: `cloudflare-dns` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`, `hostname`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `zone_id` | string | yes | — | The zone's id (32 hex characters, on the zone's Overview page). Matches `^[0-9a-f]{32}$`. |
| `name` | string | yes | — | The record's full name, lower-case, zone included. Matches `^[a-z0-9*_.-]+$`. |
| `target` | string | yes | — | The host the name points at (the record's `content`). |
| `proxied` | boolean | no | `false` | Whether Cloudflare proxies the traffic. |
| `ttl` | integer | no | `1` | TTL in seconds (60–86400), or 1 for automatic. |
| `comment` | string | no | — | A note on the record; no effect on DNS. |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: dns_cname
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: cloudflare.dns_cname
  zone_id: 023e105f4ecef8ad9ca31a8372d0c353
  name: ${ctx.scope}.preview.example.com
  target: preview-host.example.net
  comment: Managed by Sponson
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
find:
  path: /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records?type=CNAME&name.exact={name}
  list_path: /result
  match:
    type: CNAME
    name: { param: name }
create:
  path: /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records
update:
  method: PATCH
  path: /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records/{id}
  body:
    type: CNAME
    name: { param: name }
delete:
  path: /zones/{zone_id}/dns_records/{id}
item_path: /result
fields:
  content: { param: target }
  proxied: { param: proxied }
  ttl: { param: ttl }
  comment: { param: comment }
outputs:
  hostname: /name
```

## Turso

Recipe file: [`packages/adapters/recipes/turso.yaml`](../packages/adapters/recipes/turso.yaml). Verified on 2026-10-11 against:

- [Create database](https://docs.turso.tech/api-reference/databases/create)
- [Retrieve database](https://docs.turso.tech/api-reference/databases/retrieve)
- [Delete database](https://docs.turso.tech/api-reference/databases/delete)
- [Branching](https://docs.turso.tech/features/branching)

| API default | Value |
|---|---|
| `base_url` | `https://api.turso.tech/v1` |
| `base_url_env` | `TURSO_API_URL` |
| Credential | `TURSO_API_TOKEN` (bearer) |

Assumptions:

- **TU1** (verified, [source](https://docs.turso.tech/api-reference/databases/create)): `POST /v1/organizations/{organizationSlug}/databases` with `name`, `group` and `seed: { type: database, name: <parent> }` creates a database copied from the parent, authenticated with a Platform API token as `Authorization: Bearer`.
- **TU2** (verified, [source](https://docs.turso.tech/api-reference/databases/create)): The create answers `{ database: { DbId, Hostname, Name } }` (capitalised), and 409 when a database with that name exists already.
- **TU3** (verified, [source](https://docs.turso.tech/api-reference/databases/retrieve)): `GET /v1/organizations/{organizationSlug}/databases/{databaseName}` answers `{ database: { Name, DbId, Hostname, group, … } }`, and 404 when there is none.
- **TU4** (verified, [source](https://docs.turso.tech/api-reference/databases/delete)): `DELETE` on the same path removes the database; 404 when it is gone.
- **TU5** (verified, [source](https://docs.turso.tech/api-reference/databases/create)): Database names are lower-case letters, numbers and dashes, at most 64 characters, unique in the organization; the group must exist already.
- **TU6** **(unverified)**: The database is usable as soon as the create answers (no readiness to poll for a branch of a database in the same group).

### `turso.database_branch`

**Database branch** (`http.resource`). A database copied from a parent database (a branch), named for the scope, such as `app-pr-42` from `app`. Its hostname is an output for the app's connection URL. Only its existence is compared for drift: changing `group` or `parent` later does not move or re-copy a database that exists.

Covers: `turso-database` in [the coverage matrix](coverage.md#coverage-matrix). Outputs: `id`, `hostname`, `db_id`. On destroy: deleted (`destroy: keep` on the line leaves it).

| Param | Type | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `organization` | string | yes | — | The organization (or user account) slug. |
| `name` | string | yes | — | The new database's name. Matches `^[a-z0-9-]{1,64}$`. |
| `parent` | string | yes | — | The parent database to copy. |
| `group` | string | no | `default` | The group the database is placed in; it must exist. |
| `timestamp` | string | no | — | Copy the parent as it was at this ISO 8601 time (point-in-time recovery window only). |

```yaml
# under changes: (no provider block needed)
- id: database_branch
  adapter: http
  op: resource
  recipe: turso.database_branch
  organization: acme
  name: app-${ctx.scope}
  parent: app
```

What the line expands into: the [`http.resource`](plan-format.md#httpresource) params, `{ param: <name> }` standing for a param's value and `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

```yaml
read:
  path: /organizations/{organization}/databases/{name}
create:
  path: /organizations/{organization}/databases
  body:
    name: { param: name }
    group: { param: group }
    seed:
      type: database
      name: { param: parent }
      timestamp: { param: timestamp }
item_path: /database
id_path: /Name
outputs:
  hostname: /Hostname
  db_id: /DbId
```
